title: Jonas cares for the glasshouse (paraphrase)
topic: A gardener named Jonas tends a greenhouse in spring: dry soil, a hose, bees, compost, the first blossoms
tail_E: Before going home, Jonas gives each thirsty plant a drink of
target_note: Same target as formulation A: 'water' is predictable from the context (parched ground after seven warm days, a long hose between the beds, a gardener about to go home) and the tail 'gives each thirsty plant a drink of'; the word 'water' and its German equivalents (Wasser, gießen) occur nowhere in the units or in the tail. ' water' is a single Pythia token (id 1824); Pythia-160m ranks it first after the all-English context (p ~ 0.46), after the all-German context (p ~ 0.44) and after the tail alone (p ~ 0.80): as in formulation A the target is carried mainly by the tail ('a drink of'), so the context effect is expected to be smaller than in F02/F03.
author: LS-NEQ stimulus authoring (F04B, gardener Jonas, paraphrase)
notes: Formulation B: independent re-phrasing of the ten meaning units of F04A in both languages (same events, same order, same name Jonas). 'greenhouse' becomes 'glasshouse'/'Treibhaus', 'soil' becomes 'ground'/'Erde', 'neighbour' becomes 'the man next door'/'der Mann von nebenan', 'bees fly' becomes 'bees buzz'/'summen', 'blossoms open' becomes 'flowers appear'/'erscheinen', 'in the evening' becomes 'after sunset'/'nach Sonnenuntergang'. No separable verbs ('abschneiden', 'hereinkommen', 'aufgehen' avoided). Unit 9 reads naturally in German; units 1 and 10 read naturally in English.
